t.1.114.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Gāndhārī's embryo had been carried for a full year, O Janamejaya, Kuntī summoned the imperishable Dharma for the sake of conceiving a child.
t.1.114.2: The queen quickly brought an offering to Dharma, and she duly recited the incantation that Durvāsas had given her long ago.
t.1.114.3: Having united with Dharma, who had assumed a form through yogic power, the fair-hipped woman obtained a son, the best of all living beings.
t.1.114.5: In due time Kuntī gave birth to a son of abundant glory. The very moment that son was born, a bodiless voice spoke.
t.1.114.4: When the moon was joined with the asterism of Indra, in the eighth muhūrta called Abhijit, by day, when the sun stood at the midpoint of the sky, on a holy and revered lunar day.
t.1.114.6: This one will be the best of the upholders of dharma, there is no doubt; known as Yudhiṣṭhira, he is the firstborn son of Pāṇḍu.
t.1.114.7: He will be a renowned king, famed throughout the three worlds, endowed with glory, with splendor, and with virtuous conduct.
t.1.114.8: Having obtained that righteous son, Pāṇḍu spoke to her again: "They say the kṣatriya order is foremost in strength; choose a son who is foremost in strength."
t.1.114.10: When he too was born, mighty and unshakable, a voice addressed him, O Bhārata: "This one is born the best of all the strong."
t.1.114.11: And this most wondrous thing happened when Vṛkodara had just been born: having fallen from his mother's lap, he shattered a rock to powder with his limbs.
t.1.114.9: Then, thus addressed by her husband, she summoned Vāyu himself; and from that was born the mighty-armed Bhīma, of terrible prowess.
t.1.114.12: Kuntī, they say, alarmed by fear of a tiger, sprang up suddenly and did not notice Vṛkodara sleeping on her lap.
t.1.114.13: How did that boy, hard as a mass of thunderbolts, fall upon the mountain? As he fell, the rock was shattered into a hundred pieces by his limbs. Seeing that rock crushed to powder, Pāṇḍu was filled with wonder.
t.1.114.14: On the very day that Bhīma was born, O best of the Bharatas, on that same day Duryodhana too was born, O lord of the earth.
t.1.114.15: When Vṛkodara had been born, Pāṇḍu reflected further upon this: "How might I have an excellent son, one who would be the best in the world?"
t.1.114.16: For this world rests upon both fate and human effort. Of these, fate is obtained through rites performed at the proper time.
t.1.114.17: For Indra, the king of the gods, is the foremost, so we have heard; he is of immeasurable strength and energy, mighty, and of boundless splendor.
t.1.114.19: Then the mighty Pāṇḍu, the Kauravya, having taken counsel with the great seers, prescribed for Kuntī an auspicious vow lasting one year.
t.1.114.18: Having pleased him with austerity, I shall obtain a son of great strength. The son whom he gives me will be the most excellent; therefore I shall practise great austerity in deed, in mind, and in speech.
t.1.114.20: And the mighty-armed one himself stood on one foot; he undertook fierce austerity with supreme concentration.
t.1.114.21: Wishing to win the favour of that god, the lord of the thirty gods, the righteous-souled one turned round along with the sun, O Bhārata.
t.1.114.22: But after a long time Vāsava answered him: "I shall give you a son renowned throughout the three worlds."
t.1.114.23: I shall give you a foremost son, one who will accomplish the aims of the gods, of the brāhmaṇas, and of his friends, and who will destroy all his enemies.
t.1.114.24: Thus addressed by the great-souled Vāsava, the Kaurava king, righteous in spirit, remembering the words of the king of the gods, spoke to Kuntī.
t.1.114.26: Bear a son, O lovely-hipped one, an abode of the splendors of kṣatriyas. The favor has been obtained from the lord of the gods; summon him, O you of bright smiles.
t.1.114.27: Thus addressed, the illustrious lady then summoned Śakra; and the lord of the gods came and begot Arjuna.
t.1.114.25: One skilled in statecraft and great-souled, with splendor equal to the sun's, hard to assail, vigorous in action, and of an exceedingly wondrous appearance.
t.1.114.28: As soon as the boy was born, a bodiless voice spoke then, with a deep and mighty resonance, making the sky resound.
t.1.114.29: O Kuntī, this one, equal to Kārtavīrya and matching Śibi in valor, invincible like Śakra, will spread your fame far and wide.
t.1.114.30: Just as the joy of Aditi was increased by Viṣṇu, so will Arjuna, equal to Viṣṇu, increase your joy.
t.1.114.32: Through the might of his arms, the oblation-bearer Agni will attain supreme satisfaction in the Khāṇḍava forest with the fat of all creatures.
t.1.114.31: Having brought under his sway the Madras and the Kurus together with the Kekayas, as well as the Cedis, Kāśis and Karūṣas, he will firmly uphold the emblem of the Kurus.
t.1.114.34: O Kuntī, equal to Jāmadagnya and with valor like that of Viṣṇu, this one will be the foremost of the mighty, unconquered.
t.1.114.33: And this mighty hero, a leader of men, having conquered the kings of the earth, will, together with his brothers, perform three great sacrifices.
t.1.114.35: Likewise he will bring back all the divine weapons, and this bull among men will recover the fortune that was lost.
t.1.114.36: During the birth of Kuntī's son, Vāyu spoke these most wondrous words in the sky, and Kuntī heard those words of his.
t.1.114.38: And so, in the sky, there arose a tumultuous sound of the divine seers, of the heaven-dwellers together with Indra, and of the kettledrums.
t.1.114.37: When they heard that voice proclaimed so loudly, supreme joy arose among the ascetics who dwelt on Śataśṛṅga.
t.1.114.39: A great clamor arose, accompanied by showers of flowers, and the hosts of the gods, gathering together, paid homage to Pārtha.
t.1.114.40: The sons of Kadrū and the sons of Vinatā, the Gandharvas and Apsarases likewise, all the lords of creatures, and the seven great seers as well.
t.1.114.43: Wearing celestial garlands and garments and adorned with every ornament, the Apsarases sing to Bībhatsu and dance before him; and the illustrious Tumburu, together with the Gandharvas, sang forth.
t.1.114.41: Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa and Gautama, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni and Vasiṣṭha came, and the blessed Atri too, he who had risen when the sun had vanished, came here.
t.1.114.42: Marīci and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu, and Dakṣa the Prajāpati, and likewise the Gandharvas and Apsarases were there.
t.1.114.44: Bhīmasena and Ugrasena, Ūrṇāyu and likewise Anagha, Gopati and Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Sūryavarcas as the seventh.
t.1.114.45: Yugapa, Tṛṇapa, Kārṣṇi, Nandi, and likewise Citraratha; the thirteenth was Śāliśiras, and Parjanya was the fourteenth.
t.1.114.46: Kali was the fifteenth here, and Nārada the sixteenth; and there were Sadvā, Bṛhadvā, Bṛhaka, and Karāla of great renown.
t.1.114.48: And the renowned Hahā and Hūhū, the two endowed with sweetness of song: these divine Gandharvas sang there of that bull among men.
t.1.114.49: Likewise the Apsarases, joyful and adorned with every ornament, those illustrious long-eyed ones, danced and sang.
t.1.114.47: Brahmacārin, Bahuguṇa, and the renowned Suparṇa, Viśvāvasu and Bhumanyu, and likewise Sucandra as the tenth.
t.1.114.50: Anūnā and Anavadyā, the foremost of the beloved ones, Guṇāvarā and Adrikā, and likewise Sācī, Miśrakeśī and Alambusā.
t.1.114.52: Asitā and Subāhu, Supriyā and Suvapus as well, Puṇḍarīkā and Sugandhā, Surathā and Pramāthinī.
t.1.114.53: Kāmyā and Śāradvatī too danced there in troupes, as did Menakā, Sahajanyā, Parṇikā, and Puñjikasthalā.
t.1.114.51: Marīci and Śicukā, Vidyutparṇā and Tilottamā, Agnikā, Lakṣaṇā, Kṣemā, the goddess Rambhā, and Manoramā.
t.1.114.54: Kratusthalā and Ghṛtācī, Viśvācī and Pūrvacittī too, the one renowned as Umlocā, and Pramlocā: these were ten, with Urvaśī the eleventh; these long-eyed ones sang.
t.1.114.55: Dhātṛ and Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa, Aṃśa and Bhaga as well, Indra, Vivasvant and Pūṣan, Tvaṣṭṛ and Savitṛ likewise.
t.1.114.57: Mṛgavyādha and Śarva and the greatly renowned Nirṛti, Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, and Pinākī, the scorcher of foes.
t.1.114.56: Parjanya and Viṣṇu, and the Ādityas blazing like fire, stood in the sky, magnifying the greatness of the Pāṇḍava.
t.1.114.58: Dahana, and Īśvara too, and Kapālin, O lord of the people, Sthāṇu and the blessed Bhava: these Rudras stood there.
t.1.114.59: The two Aśvins, the eight Vasus, the mighty Maruts, the Viśvedevas and likewise the Sādhyas were standing there all around.
t.1.114.60: Karkoṭaka, then Śeṣa, and the serpent Vāsuki, Kacchapa and Apakuṇḍa, and the great serpent Takṣaka.
t.1.114.61: They came, endowed with fiery energy, of great wrath and great strength; these and many other Nāgas stood assembled there.
t.1.114.62: Tārkṣya and Ariṣṭanemi, Garuḍa and Asitadhvaja, Aruṇa and Āruṇi too, the sons of Vinatā, stood there in their places.
t.1.114.63: Seeing that great wonder, the best of sages were amazed, and from then on they conducted themselves with even greater regard toward the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.114.64: But the greatly renowned Pāṇḍu, out of longing for sons, once again urged her of lovely limbs; Kuntī, however, then said to him:
t.1.114.65: Even in times of distress, they do not speak of a fourth conception beyond this. Beyond this a woman would be wanton, and at a fifth she would become a harlot.
t.1.114.66: So how is it, O learned one, that you, transgressing this law that is to be grasped by the understanding, speak to me for the sake of offspring as if out of heedlessness?
